sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Choose the two correct words to fill in the blank (nodules, nodes, nodulins): (a) In legumes, nitrogen fixation occurs in specialised bodies called ______. (b) ______ is the special protein formed as a result of symbiosis in legumes.
questions.answer: (a) nodules. (b) Leghemoglobin (the nodulins help to establish the symbiosis and maintain nodule function).

questions.q: Match: (a) Azotobacter (b) Clostridium (c) Anabaena (d) Lichens with (i) anaerobic fixer (ii) aerobic fixer (iii) aerobic cyanobacterium (iv) symbiotic fixer.
Name the enzymes for: (a) nitrate to nitrite (b) nitrite to ammonia.

Name the amino acid formed by reductive amination of (a) alpha-ketoglutaric acid (b) oxaloacetic acid.
Name the organisms that fix nitrogen in (a) lichens (b) Cycas.
What is the percentage of nitrogen in the air by volume? Name the source of Chile saltpetre.
questions.answer: 78 per cent. Chile saltpetre is sodium nitrate.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the function of leghemoglobin in root nodules?
questions.answer: It acts as an oxygen scavenger, lowering the oxygen level so that nitrogenase works under anaerobic conditions.

questions.q: Distinguish between biological and abiological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: Biological fixation occurs in living cells through nitrogenase; abiological fixation occurs without living cells, industrially (Haber's process) or naturally (lightning).

questions.q: Name two conditions required for biological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: A strong reducing power (NADH2) with ATP and the enzyme nitrogenase under anaerobic conditions.

questions.q: What are nodulins?
questions.answer: Proteins synthesised in legume nodules that help in establishing the symbiosis and maintaining nodule functioning.

questions.q: State the role of transaminases.
questions.answer: They transfer an amino group from an amino acid to a keto acid, forming new amino acids.

questions.q: How do plants avoid the toxic effect of ammonia?
questions.answer: They quickly combine it with keto acids to form amino acids.

questions.q: What is Haber's process?
questions.answer: Industrial fixation: N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3 at about 500 degrees Celsius and 1000 atmospheres over an iron oxide catalyst.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the schematic representation of the nitrogen cycle.
questions.answer: Atmospheric N2 → NH3 by lightning and nitrogen-fixing bacteria (nitrogen fixation); NH3 → nitrite → nitrate by nitrifying bacteria; nitrate → plants → animals; dead organisms and excreta → NH3 by decomposers (ammonification); nitrate → N2 by denitrifying bacteria (denitrification).

questions.q: Explain symbiotic nitrogen fixation in legumes.
questions.answer: Rhizobium infects the roots and forms nodules; the nodule contains leghemoglobin, which removes oxygen so that nitrogenase can reduce N2 to NH3 using ATP and reducing power from the host, and the ammonia is converted to amino acids.

questions.q: Explain the assimilation of nitrate by plants.
questions.answer: Nitrate is reduced to nitrite by nitrate reductase in the cytosol and nitrite is reduced to ammonia by nitrite reductase in the chloroplast; the ammonia is then used in amino acid synthesis.

questions.q: Describe the two reactions of amino acid synthesis in plants.
questions.answer: Reductive amination: alpha-ketoglutaric acid + NH3 gives glutamic acid. Transamination: alpha-ketoglutaric acid + aspartic acid gives glutamic acid + oxaloacetic acid, using transaminase.

questions.q: Name any three free-living nitrogen-fixing organisms with their nature.
Write short notes on abiological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: Industrial fixation through Haber's process and natural fixation by lightning, which forms oxides of nitrogen that are converted into nitrites and nitrates.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the mechanism of biological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: It needs N2, reducing power (NADH2 and FADH2), ATP, nitrogenase and a trap for ammonia. N2 is reduced stepwise to diimide, hydrazine and then 2NH3 with 16 ATP; the ammonia is combined with organic acids to form amino acids.

questions.q: Explain the nitrogen cycle with a flow chart.
questions.answer: Nitrogen fixation (by lightning and bacteria) to ammonia, nitrification to nitrates, absorption by plants, passage to animals, decay to ammonia and denitrification back to N2.

questions.q: Explain nitrate and ammonia assimilation and amino acid synthesis in plants.
questions.answer: Nitrate is reduced to nitrite and then ammonia by two enzymes; the ammonia is used in reductive amination and transamination to form glutamic acid and other amino acids.
